text:
taylor: Heads-up — sample-app CI started failing auth after key rotation. Local `rw sample run` works because I exported new REDWOOD_API_KEY, but CI uses org token and fails with 401.

jamie: Is CI using the credentials file or env? We had two patterns floating around: pipeline writes `~/.redwood/credentials` or sets REDWOOD_API_KEY. Which one does the sample-app template recommend?

taylor: The template uses `credentials` file by default to avoid leaking envs in logs. Our infra rotates org tokens via Vault so the file is replaced every rotation. CI never restarts the runner so the process keeps the old token.

lee: That's a known race — long-lived runners + file replacement. Two mitigations: (1) have the client detect mtime/file-hash changes and reload on next request, (2) prefer ephemeral env injection at job runtime. For minimal change, client-side reload is safer.

nina: SDK parity note: Go SDK currently only reads REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Node/TS reads REDWOOD_API_KEY + RW_API_KEY and accepts `redwood_profile` for file. Python reads credentials file but only when no env var present. We need a unified precedence doc.

taylor: For CI specifically, if the runner writes the credentials file atomically (write tmp file + mv) we could detect inode change and reload. But some runners mount secrets as inodes that don't change on update (k8s projected volume). Not always reliable.

jamie: Suggestion: implement two changes: 1) SDK/CLI should check file mtime/inode/hash each request (or every N seconds) and reload if changed; 2) provide an explicit `redwood auth reload` that operators can call in CI after token rotation step.

lee: Small pseudocode for 1):
```
state = read_credentials()
last_sig = stat(file).st_ino + stat(file).st_mtime
for req in requests:
    cur_sig = stat(file).st_ino + stat(file).st_mtime
    if cur_sig != last_sig:
        state = read_credentials()
        last_sig = cur_sig
    use state.token
```

nina: Also we should standardize aliases: accept REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_API_KEY, and REDWOOD_TOKEN for the next two releases, log a deprecation warning if alias used. Document canonical: REDWOOD_API_KEY.

taylor: Another wrinkle: project-scoped vs org-scoped tokens. CI uses org-scoped for cross-project deploys. We need to log the scope type when auth fails (no secrets) so teams know mismatch. Example message: "401: token invalid or rotated (detected token source: file; expected org-scoped). Run `redwood auth reload` or update REDWOOD_API_KEY."

ci-bot: ci-check: sample-app/integration 1805001128 — auth 401 during deploy step.

jamie: Also add a tiny health-check endpoint in sample-app templates that calls `redwood whoami` and fails fast if auth is bad; CI step can call it post-rotation. Cheap guardrail.

lee: For private deployments with managed rotation (Vault/HSM), add `redwood auth --sync-managed` to attempt rotation handshake and surface instructions if it can't renew automatically.

nina: I'll draft an RFC for env-var precedence + aliases + runtime reload behavior. Include telemetry events: auth_failure.reason=(rotated|invalid|missing), auth_source=(env|file|managed), and omit any token values.

taylor: Action items: nina RFC (env+reload+telemetry), jamie + lee implement reload + `auth reload` in CLI and add integration test that simulates in-place file swap and k8s projected volume behavior. I'll update sample-app CI recipe to call `redwood auth reload` after secret rotation job.

jamie: I'll scope the PR: CLI + Node+Python SDK parity for alias handling, file mtime/inode reload, and a minimal integration test. Targeting patch release.

lee: I'll add the whoami health-check to templates and a CI job stub.

taylor: Thanks — this will save a bunch of onboarding headache for teams using managed rotation. :raised_hands:
